canonicalisationSchema.v1Defect: B-FI-09. v1 named levels but published no byte-level construction, so two independent producers could implement different hashes and both claim conformance — destroying exactly the cross-version and cross-platform identity stability the ladder exists to provide.

construction.step1: Extract the body span at L0 byte boundaries.
construction.step2: For L0, the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes with no tokenisation. For L1-L3, apply the level's declared transform to the versioned language token stream. Token boundaries, canonical kind IDs, and replacements are part of the level-version specification.
construction.step3: Serialise the selected payload with the byteGrammar below: raw length-prefixed bytes for L0, or a count-framed stream of length-prefixed canonical kind/value byte pairs for L1-L3.
construction.step4: Hash with DOMAIN SEPARATION over a FULLY FRAMED preimage: H(len-prefixed domainTag || len-prefixed levelId || len-prefixed levelVersion || len-prefixed languageId || len-prefixed languageVersion || len-prefixed payload). Unframed concatenation of the identity components is FORBIDDEN (R2-FI-03).

canonicalisationSchema.collisionPolicy: A hash collision between two distinct canonical payloads is a HOST DEFECT, reported as such and never resolved by preferring one. Framing makes distinct canonical payloads produce distinct preimages; an intended normalisation equivalence may map different source spans to the same canonical payload.
canonicalisationSchema.goldenCorpusRequirement: Each implementation must supply a versioned corpus for every language it admits, including adversarial significant whitespace, comment-shaped directives, string literals containing comment syntax, Unicode normalisation, and mixed line endings. TypeScript and Rust are required for v1; other matrix rows require evidence before a later product admission. FI-CANON checks that this obligation remains declared; retained corpus contents and execution records are implementation/qualification evidence, not architecture evidence fabricated by this checker.

byteGrammar.encoding: UTF-8 source bytes as read from the snapshot; no re-encoding
byteGrammar.unicodeNormalization: none at L0; NFC only if a level transform explicitly declares it
byteGrammar.lineEndings: L0 preserves CR/LF/CRLF as in the snapshot bytes; L1+ may normalise only where the language treats them as insignificant whitespace
byteGrammar.bodySpanBoundary: half-open byte offsets [start,end) into the snapshot file blob; end exclusive
byteGrammar.levelVersionDefinition: raw 32-byte SHA-256 content digest of the canonical level specification, including per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order, and replacement byte rules; a human semantic-version label alone is insufficient

identifierEncoding.domainTag: exact ASCII bytes of the fixed domainTag literal
identifierEncoding.levelId: exact ASCII bytes of the enumerated normalisationLadder.level value
identifierEncoding.levelVersion: raw 32-byte digest defined by levelVersionDefinition, not hexadecimal display text
identifierEncoding.languageId: lowercase ASCII bytes of the languageCapability.matrix language id
identifierEncoding.languageVersion: exact canonical identity bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string

payloadEncodingByLevel.L0-verbatim: u32be raw_byte_len || exact snapshot body-span bytes; tokenisation is forbidden

byteGrammar.tokenKindDefinition: kind_id is the non-empty UTF-8 canonical identifier from the token-kind registry committed by levelVersion; producer/toolchain numeric enum ordinals are forbidden
byteGrammar.tokenValueDefinition: value_bytes are the exact source lexeme bytes unless the level specification replaces them with declared canonical ASCII bytes; no implicit Unicode or encoding conversion is permitted
byteGrammar.tokenEncoding: each token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id_bytes || u32be value_len || value_bytes
byteGrammar.languageVersionDefinition: the language toolchain/mode identity recorded in PlanId / ResolvedInputs for the provider interpreting the body span (e.g. typescript@X, rustc@Y edition Z); this identity remains framed for L0 even though its payload is raw bytes
byteGrammar.forbidden: raw string concatenation of levelId||levelVersion||languageId||languageVersion without length prefixes; tokenising L0; raw producer/toolchain numeric token-kind ordinals

normalisationLadder.form: A ladder of named, independently versioned levels, not one policy.
normalisationLadder.why: Exact-duplicate and near-duplicate detection want different normalisation; forcing one loses precision or recall permanently.

levels.normalises: nothing — raw bytes of the body span
L2 plus consistent renaming of LOCAL bindings

rules.rule: Each level is separately versioned. Changing L2's comment grammar does not touch L1 identities.
The level and its version are part of the fact's identity and enter the derivation key. Two levels are two facts, never one fact computed differently.
A finding records the level that produced it. Comparing a baseline entry pinned to L1 against an L2 result is a typed mismatch, not a diff.
Adding a level is schema-additive and changes no existing identity.
Changing an EXISTING level's algorithm requires the custody transition protocol below. There is no migrator that can invent the old identity from the new one.
The L0 span LOCATION is retrievable for any finding at any level. Retrieving its BYTES is a separate, retention-governed act (B-FI-04).

factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1.purpose: Keep normalized source-body identity and generic admitted-fact identity as two composable contracts. A clone payload may carry a normalized body identity; the host then mints a distinct FACT-ID-V1 for the complete admitted fact record.

normalizedBodyIdentity.input: one normalized source body span plus level/language/version components

genericFactRecordIdentity.input: the exact fourteen-field admitted FactRecordV1 semantic preimage

clonePayloadJoin.rule: The normalized body identity is payload data inside a clones fact. FACT-ID-V1 wraps the complete clone fact and can never equal or substitute for bodyIdentity by type or domain.

separationRules: The two domain tags and contract identifiers are distinct and immutable within v1.
Normalized body identity never hashes FactEnvelope, relation payload, universes, confidence or anchors.
FACT-ID-V1 never re-runs body normalization; it hashes the already validated relation payload bytes and anchors, including bodyIdentity only when the relation schema carries it.
A provider may compute a candidate bodyIdentity under the pinned body grammar but never mints FACT-ID-V1; the host validates both boundaries.
factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1.assurance: IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED; exact FACT-ID-V1 vectors live in FACT-PLANE and normalized-body corpora remain implementation evidence

languageCapability.rule: Each level is implementable per language at a declared capability. A language that cannot implement a level MUST report Coverage with the fact-plane deficiency vocabulary — never a silent approximation.

matrix.note: R2-FI-05: L2/L3 full only after directive/JSDoc corpora; provisional until then.
Indentation is SIGNIFICANT, so L1 may not normalise leading whitespace. L3 needs binding resolution beyond the syntax tier.
Build-constraint comments are directives, not comments. R2-FI-05: semicolon insertion requires token-aware L1; provisional until measured.

languageCapability.significantLayoutRule: A level MUST NOT normalise layout that is semantically significant in the target language. Python indentation is the canonical case; anything inside a string literal is universal.
languageCapability.directiveRule: Comment-shaped DIRECTIVES are classified separately from removable comments and are NEVER removed at L2. Examples: Go build constraints, TypeScript triple-slash references and ts-ignore, Rust inner attributes and doc comments feeding cfg, Python encoding declarations and type comments. Removing a directive changes meaning, so removing it at a level advertised as comment-insensitive would make two semantically different bodies identical.
neverNormalise: layout that is significant in the language

capabilityGrades.full: the contract requires full language semantics; an implementation may advertise this grade only after adversarial golden-corpus agreement across two producers
capabilityGrades.full-provisional: judgment from language spec; MUST be treated as restricted for shipping identity claims until measured
capabilityGrades.restricted: known semantic caveats; identity equivalence only within declared constraints
capabilityGrades.unavailable: must emit language-tier-unsupported deficiency; never silent approximation

languageCapability.productScopeRule: supportedLanguages is the architecture capability matrix, not the v1 installed-language set. v1 admits TypeScript and Rust only. Python or Go identity production requires an explicit later product scope change plus the corresponding corpus evidence before admission.
languageCapability.bindingRule: Exactly one matrix row per supportedLanguages entry. Every (language, level) cell MUST have a levelFixture whose expected capability equals the matrix cell (full-provisional may fixture as restricted for shipping behavior). Deleting a row or desynchronizing a fixture fails FI-CAP (R2-FI-02).
